On Apr 9, 2010, at 6:10 PM, <mauede at alice.it> <mauede at alice.it> wrote:

> I recently updated R on Linus/SuSE 11.1
> I complained because no on-line help was available from JGR after R update. I was told to update JGR as well.
> How can I do that ?
> I installed JGR on SuSE three times in the past with different R versions.Every time it's been a nightmare.
> I am afraid to have to spend a whole day, maybe longer, to update JGR ...
> I would greatly appreciate some clear guidelines for JGR installation/update on SuSE.
> Thank you in advance.

The upgrade should be trivial as long as your system is properly setup - simply run

update.packages(ask=FALSE, checkBuilt=TRUE)

that works for all packages. If that fails then either R or Java on your system are not setup properly.

Instructions for installing JGR from scratch on SuSE are at
http://jgr.markushelbig.org/JGR_on_Linux.html

If all that doesn't help all I can say if you want easier setup get a more user-firendy distro or system ;).

Cheers,
Simon

Hi,

I have a Java application/database which manages R object code portions and their revision.
I would like to make use of JGR as a way to both run and edit the code portions.

Problems:
a) Is it possible to instantiate a JGR object in java?
When I do the following I get a frame but the app stalls then without fully rendering JGR:
JGR jgr = new JGR();
Is this because it cannot find the jgr.dll?
Is there any documentation / example code on doing this sort of stuff?

b) Is the source for the JGR java code available and if so where?  I downloaded the JGR source tarball from rforge but it only contains the jgr.jar file with compiled classes.

c) I can instantiate the JGR Editor and setText() into it but is there a way to getText() from it?
I guess I can extend the class and add a listener for the close event?   Again the source would help me.

c) When I close the Editor object from within the interface it must do an exit() as it shuts down my app.  Is their a way to modify this behaviour?
I tried setting setDefaultCloseOperation to DISPOSE_ON_CLOSE or even DO_NOTHING_ON_CLOSE but to no avail.


Thanks all

Troy

On Apr 15, 2010, at 2:32 AM, Troy Robertson wrote:

> I have a Java application/database which manages R object code portions and their revision.
> I would like to make use of JGR as a way to both run and edit the code portions.
> 
> Problems:
> a) Is it possible to instantiate a JGR object in java?


Yes - see the JGR source (that's almost exactly what the main() method does). You just have to make sure that you setup the environment properly to run R. The easiest way to do that is to use the JGR launcher which does it automatically.


> When I do the following I get a frame but the app stalls then without fully rendering JGR:
> JGR jgr = new JGR();
> Is this because it cannot find the jgr.dll?

There is no JGR.dll. See instructions for JRI. The recommended way (which is what JGR does) is to use RJavaClassLoader and let it run the main method (see the java command used by the launcher).


> Is there any documentation / example code on doing this sort of stuff?
> 

JGR itself - since that's what you want to do I suppose. (Although I'm not quite sure I understand why since the common approach is the other way round since any Java code can be run from JGR trivially).


> b) Is the source for the JGR java code available and if so where?  I downloaded the JGR source tarball from rforge but it only contains the jgr.jar file with compiled classes.

Yes, see svn://svn.rforge.net/org/trunk/rosuda/JGR/

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

For the xlsx package, I am exploring how to add R generated plots to an 
xlsx document (it should be possible).  In doing that I need to call the 
method "toByteArray" from
http://poi.apache.org/apidocs/org/apache/poi/util/IOUtils.html
and I don't know how to set the return signature for a byte array.

I've tried "[B" but it does not work.  See below for some commented code.

Thank you,
Adrian

Here are the full details, not all are needed...

   wb <- createWorkbook()
   sheet <- createSheet(wb, "Sheet1")

   # I have a jpeg file
   picname <- paste(.Library, "/xlsx/tests/log_plot.jpeg", sep="")
   pic_ext <- paste("PICTURE_TYPE_",
     toupper(gsub(".*\\.(.*)$", "\\1", picname)), sep="")


   iStream <- .jnew("java/io/FileInputStream", picname)
   # why if I use "Lorg/apache/poi/util/IOUtils;" errors out?
   ioutils <- .jnew("org/apache/poi/util/IOUtils")
   #jbytes <- .jcall(ioutils, "[B", "toByteArray", iStream) # Error: [B not 
found
   bytes <- ioutils$toByteArray(iStream)  # read the picture as R raw
   iStream$close()

   # as I don't know how to create the byte array directly, so I do it
   # below using R's raw.  Does not create a "proper" xlsx file.
   # plot is not displayed.
   jbytes <- .jarray(bytes)  # creates an array of bytes from R's raw

   extId <- .jfield(wb, "I", pic_ext)
   # here I add the picture as a byte array to the workbook...
   picId <- .jcall(wb, "I", "addPicture", jbytes, as.integer(extId))

   drawing <- .jcall(sheet,
     "Lorg/apache/poi/xssf/usermodel/XSSFDrawing;", 
"createDrawingPatriarch")

   factory <- .jcall(wb,
     "Lorg/apache/poi/xssf/usermodel/XSSFCreationHelper;", 
"getCreationHelper")
   anchor <- .jcall(factory,
     "Lorg/apache/poi/ss/usermodel/ClientAnchor;", "createClientAnchor")
   .jcall(anchor, "V", "setCol1", as.integer(1))
   .jcall(anchor, "V", "setRow1", as.integer(1))
   # here I display the picture.
   pict <- .jcall(drawing, "Lorg/apache/poi/xssf/usermodel/XSSFPicture;",
     "createPicture", anchor, as.integer(picId))

   file <- "C:/Temp/test_picture.xlsx"
   saveWorkbook(wb, file)
   cat("Wrote file:", file, "\n")

> 
> I've tried "[B" but it does not work.  

It does - the error is in how you pass the stream argument - see below.


> See below for some commented code.
> 
> Thank you,
> Adrian
> 
> Here are the full details, not all are needed...
> 
>   wb <- createWorkbook()
>   sheet <- createSheet(wb, "Sheet1")
> 
>   # I have a jpeg file
>   picname <- paste(.Library, "/xlsx/tests/log_plot.jpeg", sep="")
>   pic_ext <- paste("PICTURE_TYPE_",
>     toupper(gsub(".*\\.(.*)$", "\\1", picname)), sep="")
> 
> 
>   iStream <- .jnew("java/io/FileInputStream", picname)
>   # why if I use "Lorg/apache/poi/util/IOUtils;" errors out?

Because that's not a correct class name


>   ioutils <- .jnew("org/apache/poi/util/IOUtils")
>   #jbytes <- .jcall(ioutils, "[B", "toByteArray", iStream) # Error: [B not 
> found

You're not casting the stream appropriately - see:

> .jmethods(ioutils, "toByteArray")
[1] "public static byte[] org.apache.poi.util.IOUtils.toByteArray(java.io.InputStream) throws java.io.IOException"

> iStream
[1] "Java-Object{java.io.FileInputStream@4e82701e}"

So you need to cast the stream:

> bytes <- .jcall(ioutils, "[B", "toByteArray", .jcast(iStream, "java/io/InputStream"))
> str(bytes)
 raw [1:10576] ff d8 ff e0 ...

Cheers,
Simon

On Fri, 30 Apr 2010, Simon Urbanek wrote:

> Adrian,
>
> On Apr 29, 2010, at 4:33 PM, Adrian Dragulescu wrote:
>
>>
>> Hello,
>>
>> For the xlsx package, I am exploring how to add R generated plots to an
>> xlsx document (it should be possible).  In doing that I need to call the
>> method "toByteArray" from
>> http://poi.apache.org/apidocs/org/apache/poi/util/IOUtils.html
>> and I don't know how to set the return signature for a byte array.
>>
>> I've tried "[B" but it does not work.
>
> It does - the error is in how you pass the stream argument - see below.
>
>
>> See below for some commented code.
>>
>> Thank you,
>> Adrian
>>
>> Here are the full details, not all are needed...
>>
>>   wb <- createWorkbook()
>>   sheet <- createSheet(wb, "Sheet1")
>>
>>   # I have a jpeg file
>>   picname <- paste(.Library, "/xlsx/tests/log_plot.jpeg", sep="")
>>   pic_ext <- paste("PICTURE_TYPE_",
>>     toupper(gsub(".*\\.(.*)$", "\\1", picname)), sep="")
>>
>>
>>   iStream <- .jnew("java/io/FileInputStream", picname)
>>   # why if I use "Lorg/apache/poi/util/IOUtils;" errors out?
>
> Because that's not a correct class name
>
>
>>   ioutils <- .jnew("org/apache/poi/util/IOUtils")
>>   #jbytes <- .jcall(ioutils, "[B", "toByteArray", iStream) # Error: [B not
>> found
>
> You're not casting the stream appropriately - see:
>
>> .jmethods(ioutils, "toByteArray")
> [1] "public static byte[] org.apache.poi.util.IOUtils.toByteArray(java.io.InputStream) throws java.io.IOException"
>
>> iStream
> [1] "Java-Object{java.io.FileInputStream@4e82701e}"
>
> So you need to cast the stream:
>
>> bytes <- .jcall(ioutils, "[B", "toByteArray", .jcast(iStream, "java/io/InputStream"))
>> str(bytes)
> raw [1:10576] ff d8 ff e0 ...
>
> Cheers,
> Simon
>
>
>>   bytes <- ioutils$toByteArray(iStream)  # read the picture as R raw
>>   iStream$close()
>>
>>   # as I don't know how to create the byte array directly, so I do it
>>   # below using R's raw.  Does not create a "proper" xlsx file.
>>   # plot is not displayed.
>>   jbytes <- .jarray(bytes)  # creates an array of bytes from R's raw
>>
>>   extId <- .jfield(wb, "I", pic_ext)
>>   # here I add the picture as a byte array to the workbook...
>>   picId <- .jcall(wb, "I", "addPicture", jbytes, as.integer(extId))
>>
>>   drawing <- .jcall(sheet,
>>     "Lorg/apache/poi/xssf/usermodel/XSSFDrawing;",
>> "createDrawingPatriarch")
>>
>>   factory <- .jcall(wb,
>>     "Lorg/apache/poi/xssf/usermodel/XSSFCreationHelper;",
>> "getCreationHelper")
>>   anchor <- .jcall(factory,
>>     "Lorg/apache/poi/ss/usermodel/ClientAnchor;", "createClientAnchor")
>>   .jcall(anchor, "V", "setCol1", as.integer(1))
>>   .jcall(anchor, "V", "setRow1", as.integer(1))
>>   # here I display the picture.
>>   pict <- .jcall(drawing, "Lorg/apache/poi/xssf/usermodel/XSSFPicture;",
>>     "createPicture", anchor, as.integer(picId))
>>
>>   file <- "C:/Temp/test_picture.xlsx"
>>   saveWorkbook(wb, file)
>>   cat("Wrote file:", file, "\n")
>>
>>

>> stats-rosuda-devel mailing list
>> stats-rosuda-devel at listserv.uni-augsburg.de

>
